episodes.212349: A moist and unstable weather pattern affected Puerto Rico from March 24 through March 28, 2026, as a mid- to upper-level trough interacted with abundant tropical moisture and favorable upper-level dynamics. Periods of heavy showers and thunderstorms developed across the island, resulting in flooding concerns, urban and small-stream flooding, and rapid rises on rivers and streams. The threat was enhanced by strong upper-level support associated with a strengthening jet stream and persistent moisture across the region.

Heavy rainfall produced flash flooding at Ernesto Ramos Antonini School in Yauco. Floodwaters accumulated rapidly on the school grounds, causing flooding in the affected area. No injuries, fatalities, or evacuations were reported. The flooding was associated with intense rainfall that affected portions of southwestern Puerto Rico.

Heavy rainfall triggered flash flooding in southern Yauco, inundating portions of Roads 127 and 128. The roads became impassable, resulting in hazardous travel conditions and temporary transportation disruptions. No injuries, fatalities, or structural damage were reported.

Heavy rainfall caused rapid rises along a tributary crossing PR-5516 in Adjuntas. Floodwaters overtopped a bridge located between Selecto Supermarket and the Sweet and Frozen business, making the roadway impassable and disrupting local travel. No injuries or fatalities were reported.
